text:
CLINICAL FEATURES OF PITYRIASIS VERSICOLOR (TINEA VERSICOLOR)
Clinical Features
- Usually asymptomatic (or just mild itching)
- May be generalized in the immuno-compromised
- Fine scaly, guttate or nummular patches, particularly on young adults who
perspire freely
- Individual patches are dirty, yellowish/ brownish/hypopigmented macules
(hence the term versicolor)
- Larger irregular patches may evolve
- Sometimes follicular tendency is marked; more noticeable at the advancing
edges of the irregular patches
Sites of predilection:
- Sternal region
- Sides of the chest
- Shoulders
- Upper back
- Face
Differential Diagnoses
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis
- Pityriasis alba
- Pityriasis rosea
- Leprosy
